items.stem: “The Silk route was a good example of vibrant pre-modern trade and cultural links between distant parts of the world.” Explain the statement with any two examples.
items.answer: The Silk route linked distant regions in both trade and culture. (1) Spices from India and Southeast Asia were traded to Europe, and in return precious metals such as gold and silver flowed from Europe to Asia. (2) Along the same routes Christian missionaries travelled to Asia, carrying beliefs and ideas with them. Trade and cultural exchange therefore moved together along the Silk route.

items.stem: State the basic and main objectives of New Economic Policy.
items.answer: The main objectives of the New Economic Policy were: (i) to reduce domestic inflation and improve the balance of payments; and (ii) to improve efficiency and productivity and put the economy back on the path of growth with social justice.

items.stem: Which factors were responsible for price rise of foodgrains in Britain in late nineteenth century was/were ?
items.answer: The factors responsible for the rise in the price of foodgrains in Britain were: (i) increasing demand for agricultural products, (ii) increasing demand for foodgrains, and (iii) increasing population.

items.stem: List some few food items that travelled from far away places to India.
items.answer: Food items that reached India from far away places include: (i) tomato and sweet potatoes, (ii) potatoes and groundnuts, and (iii) maize and chillies.

items.stem: Name the three international institutions that work for the implementation of Globalisation.
items.answer: The three international institutions are: (i) the International Monetary Fund (IMF), (ii) the World Bank, and (iii) the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

items.stem:
Define the concept of :
(a) Market
(b) Economic barometer
items.answer: (a) Market: a market is a place where the exchange of goods takes place; several sellers and many customers bargain there, selling and purchasing various articles and services. (b) Economic barometer: advancing international trade of a country leads to its economic prosperity, and trade is therefore considered to be the economic barometer of a country.

items.stem: Why can the First World War be termed as first modern industrial war ? Give three reason.
items.answer: The First World War is called the first modern industrial war for these reasons: (a) it saw the use of machine guns, tanks, aircraft and the like, all products of modern large scale industries; (b) the scale of total death and destruction was very large; and (c) carrying millions of soldiers needed large warships and railway trains, which could only be manufactured in large scale industries.

items.stem: Define liberalisation. Mention two components of liberalisation.
items.answer: Liberalisation is the relaxation of all the rules and regulations that earlier restricted the growth of the private sector. Its two components are: (i) allowing the private sector to run industrial activities that were earlier restricted to the public sector, and (ii) relaxing all rules and regulations that restrict the growth of the private sector.

items.stem: What do you mean by the term GPL ?
items.answer: GPL stands for Globalisation, Privatisation and Liberalisation. (i) Globalisation is the merger of the economies of individual countries into a global economy. (ii) Privatisation is the transfer of ownership, control and management of almost all erstwhile public sector undertakings to the private sector, done phase-wise. (iii) Liberalisation is the removal of trade barriers by relaxing trade laws, import rules and so on — for example the creation of SEZs, with labour laws made lenient, giving way to a contract or indentured labour system.

items.stem: What do you know about WTO ? Write about it in brief (short).
items.answer: WTO stands for the World Trade Organisation. It was set up in 1995 at Geneva, Switzerland. An international institution was already working as an organisation of the UN, called GATT — the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade — set up in 1947, two years after the birth of the UNO. The WTO replaced GATT in 1995 and since then has worked independently, though attached to the UN to some extent.

items.stem:
Write any three factors (values) which played a crucial role in the decline export of Indian textiles.
or
Which three factors are responsible for the declining Indian textile export ?
items.answer: The factors that played a crucial role in the decline of Indian textile exports were: (i) the Industrial Revolution in Europe, (ii) taxes imposed on Indian textile goods, and (iii) duty free British textile goods — sent to Indian markets without any levy — which were comparably cheaper than Indian cotton made goods.

items.stem: Why did Fixed Exchange Rate system collapse in 1960s ? Give three reasons.
items.answer: The fixed exchange rate system collapsed because: (1) from the 1960s the rising cost of its overseas involvements weakened the US’s finances and competitive strength; (2) the US dollar no longer commanded confidence as the world’s principal currency; and (3) it could not maintain its value in relation to gold, which led to the collapse of the fixed exchange rates.

items.stem: Examine different factors which led people to migrate to the continents of America and Australia in the nineteenth century.
items.answer: People migrated to America and Australia in the nineteenth century because: (i) acquiring agricultural land and getting better accommodation in these continents was a powerful attraction for the poor and backward people of poor countries; and (ii) better trade, commerce and industrial opportunities in America and Australia also inspired migrants from Asia, Africa and Latin America.

items.stem: Write any three negative aspects of liberalisation and globalisation.
items.answer: Negative aspects of liberalisation and globalisation include: (i) the rate of unemployment increased beyond expectations; (ii) the growth rate declined to 4% per annum in 2002–03 from 8% in 1972–73; (iii) the laws failed to reduce the concentration of economic power in the private sector; and (iv) public sector enterprises ran into severe losses, to the tune of ₹ 203 crore, because of corruption, inefficiency and ineffective management.
